title: Something Killed 3 of My Hens Last Night. Here's How I Knew Exactly What It Was
description:
Three of my hens were dead on Tuesday morning, piled in a corner, and one was missing her head. Every predator leaves its own calling card. Here's how I read the signs — how many, where, what was eaten, how it got in — what it turned out to be, how I fixed my coop, and what it cost.

Quick guide: Raccoon — head/crop eaten, birds killed by the wire, opens simple latches. Opossum — one bird, eaten from behind; loves eggs. Skunk — eggs opened at one end. Fox/coyote — whole bird carried off, feather trail, often daytime. Hawk — circle of plucked feathers in the open, daytime. Owl — head and neck eaten, birds roosting in the open. Dog — many killed and scattered, barely eaten. Mink/weasel — several killed at once inside, bites at the back of the neck, bodies piled, through a hole the size of a quarter.

The fix: 1/2" hardware cloth (not chicken wire) screwed with washers over every opening, a buried wire apron, two-step latches, close the hen door every night at dusk.

pinned_comment:
Chicken wire keeps chickens IN — it doesn't keep predators out. 1/2" hardware cloth, screwed down with washers, on every opening. And close that door at dusk, every night. 🐔
Where are you, and what predators do you have?
